title: Search a 2D Matrix
statement_short: Given an m x n integer matrix with sorted rows where the first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row, determine if target is in the matrix in O(log(m \* n)) time.
constraints: m == matrix.length, n == matrix[i].length, 1 <= m, n <= 100, -10^4 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^4, -10^4 <= target <= 10^4
hint: O(log(m \* n)) time requirement allows flattening 2D coordinates into a virtual 1D sorted array.
keywords: first integer of each row is greater
why_not: Right: Binary Search treats the matrix as a virtual 1D sorted array using index mapping (row = mid / n, col = mid % n) in O(log(m\*n)) time. Not Two Pointers: Scanning from top-right corner works in O(m + n) time, which is slower than O(log(m\*n)) binary search. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Storing matrix entries in a set check lookups in O(1) time but uses O(m\*n) auxiliary space. Not 2D DP: Grid dynamic programming memoizes state paths rather than performing logarithmic target search.
